geos.label: South Bay
geos.blurb: San Jose, Saratoga, Sunnyvale, Mountain View

events.title: Sharks vs Flames
events.note: Calgary in for an early-season Monday. Upper-bowl seats go cheap on a weeknight and the building is a ten-minute walk from Diridon.

events.title: Santa Clara Broncos vs Towson Tigers
events.note: College basketball in a 4,700-seat box on the Santa Clara campus — the cheap, loud, walkable end of the sport, which is the only end the brief cares about.

events.title: The Psychedelic Furs with We Are Scientists
events.note: Richard Butler's voice has not softened and the band play better now than they did in the 1990s. Doors seven. Four minutes' walk from Caltrain Menlo Park, which is the way to do it. Last week's digest had this a day early; the Guild's own calendar says Monday.

events.title: Día de los Muertos Festival of Altars
events.note: Thirteen hours of community-built ofrendas in the park at 25th and Potrero, the quiet half of the Mission's Day of the Dead. Arrive after dark and the candles do the work.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Nine to ten on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays the 1894 garden is free to everybody; San Francisco residents are free any time with ID. The hour before the crowds is the one worth taking.

events.title: Día de los Muertos: 45th Annual Procession
events.note: Forty-five years of the same route: drums, calaca masks and no floats, from 22nd and Bryant through the Mission. The oldest procession of its kind in the city and still not a parade.

events.title: Lady
events.note: Off-beat comedy about a narcissistic aristocrat who traps an opportunistic director into filming her life. The Roxie's longest-running title of the autumn.

events.title: The History of Concrete
events.note: John Wilson's first feature after How To with John Wilson — the same accidental-encounter method at feature length, and much stranger for it. Holds over from last week.

events.title: Club Kid (SFFILM presents, 35mm)
events.note: SFFILM in the Castro on a 35mm print, doors at half five. The format is the reason to go — the Castro's screen and a projected print together are getting rare in this city.

events.title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night
events.note: Free with an Eventbrite RSVP, $20–$25 at the door, two-drink minimum. The Function books better comics than a free Monday has any right to.

events.title: LUCY (Cooper B. Handy) with F.G.S.
events.note: Cooper B. Handy's project — lo-fi bedroom pop that keeps collapsing into something closer to outsider rap, delivered deadpan. One of the odder bookings of the week in a 150-cap bar.

events.title: Motown on Mondays
events.note: Fifteen years of 45s on a Monday — Motown, Stax and the northern soul end of it, on vinyl. Free before eight and $5 after, which is still the cheapest dancing in the city.

events.title: The Cult of Cinema Happy Hour
events.note: A film-chat happy hour in the back of the Knockout — trailers, tangents and arguments about things nobody has seen. Free on a DICE RSVP.

events.title: Madre Cumbia: Los Gaiteros de San Jacinto, Fruko y sus Tesos, Carmelo Torres
events.note: Three generations of Colombian music on one bill: the Gaiteros carrying gaita flute tradition from the Montes de María, Fruko's salsa orchestra that defined the Discos Fuentes sound, and Carmelo Torres playing cumbia on the accordion the way Andrés Landero did. A booking that would be a festival headline anywhere else.

events.title: Lexi Jayde with Ally Salort
events.note: Conversational heartbreak pop with a guitar underneath it, from a writer who came up posting demos and has kept the plainness. Ally Salort opens.

events.title: Mirthquake: Monday Live Comedy
events.note: Free with RSVP in an Irish bar on Geary, with $5 drinks and a room small enough that the comics can hear you not laughing. 21+.

events.title: Fjord
events.note: A title in the Roxie's rotating run. The calendar gives the time and the poster and nothing else; descriptor withheld rather than guessed.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Documentary assembled from night-time rooftop conversations in Tel Aviv about the machinery behind Israel's mass targeting. Second week here.

events.title: Krazy for Karaoke
events.note: The Knockout's Monday karaoke, which is less a performance than a sport. Free on an RSVP.

events.title: Sonido Inesperable with DJ X'ces
events.note: Sonidero cumbia — the Mexico City DJ tradition where the record is the instrument and the shout-outs are the show. Listed only on the regional sweep, so the time is unconfirmed.

events.title: The Illusion of Space: Patrick Hughes
events.note: Hughes's reverspective paintings — perspective built in relief so the picture appears to turn as you walk past it. Closes on 4 November, so this is the last full week.

events.title: Town Biz Comedy Night
events.note: HellaFunny's Monday night in Temescal, free with RSVP, with mezcal and mole to buy. Runs Mondays and Tuesdays and the Monday bill is usually the looser one.

events.title: Freakyoke
events.note: Free karaoke at the Stork, which means the song list skews to things nobody should attempt. No cover.

events.title: Alexi Kenney
events.note: A violinist who programmes recitals as arguments — Bach next to living composers, with the joins left showing — in Crowden's small hall on Rose Street. Time unconfirmed.

events.title: Ivy
events.note: Listed on the regional sweep and absent from Cornerstone's own upcoming-shows page, as with three other Cornerstone bookings this week — see the digest's reachability notes.

events.title: Lee Ritenour
events.note: Fifty years of session guitar — the player on half the records you can hum from the 1970s — doing it in his own name in a 400-seat room. First of two nights.

events.title: Prince Daddy and The Hyena with Combat, Walter Etc. and Friendship Games
events.note: Albany emo at its most unembarrassed, three supports deep, in a 500-cap room. The better of the South Bay's two weeknight rock bookings.

events.title: Santa Clara Broncos vs Wisconsin-Milwaukee Panthers
events.note: The second of three Broncos home games this week.

events.title: Upstairs Downstairs Tour
events.note: The service corridors and the family rooms in one walk, which is the only way the house makes sense. An hour and a half. Filoli's holiday season does not open until 13 November, so the tours are the whole programme this week.

events.title: ARIA Concert
events.note: A promoter-sold date at the Fox: the theatre's own page carries the listing but sells no tickets for it and publishes no time or lineup.

events.title: Legion of Honor Free Day
events.note: Same museum group, same first-Tuesday rule, and the better building of the two. Advance timed tickets required.

events.title: de Young Museum Free Day
events.venue: de Young Museum, Golden Gate Park
events.note: First Tuesday of the month, general admission free to everyone, special exhibitions still charged. Timed tickets required and they go, so book the morning.

events.title: Conservatory of Flowers Free First Tuesday
events.venue: Conservatory of Flowers, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The 1879 glasshouse, free on the first Tuesday. Twenty minutes in the Highland Tropics room is worth more than most ticketed exhibitions.

events.title: Cartoon Art Museum Pay What You Wish
events.note: Pay what you wish on the first Tuesday at the only museum in the country devoted to comics and animation art. Original pages, not reproductions.

events.title: Election Night Watch Party with Kochina Rude
events.note: A drag host, bingo and the returns on the screens at a midterm night in a converted mortuary chapel. Free with RSVP, all ages, five till ten.

events.title: Los Domingos
events.note: A title in the Roxie's current run; descriptor withheld rather than guessed.

events.title: Wild at Heart (4K restoration)
events.note: Lynch's Palme d'Or winner, Cage in the snakeskin jacket, restored. Costume night — come as a character and the popcorn is free.

events.title: Outright (debut), Dog House and Kaitlyn Williams
events.note: A debut set opening a three-band local bill — the kind of night the Knockout exists for and nothing else in the city lists.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: The Mischief company's Peter Pan, in which everything that can fall off the set does. Running to 28 November; the Playhouse publishes no per-date times, so these follow the schedule the run has kept.

events.title: Thunder Clap Comedy Show
events.note: Stand-up in the Kilowatt's back room on a DICE RSVP. Free, which is the correct price for a Tuesday.

events.title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night
events.note: The Tuesday edition, free with RSVP, $20–$25 at the door, two-drink minimum.

events.title: The Marriage of Figaro
events.note: Mozart's day-long farce about class, consent and a locked door, in the second of nine performances. Four hours including intervals and worth all of them.

events.title: Two Headliner Comedy Night: Reem Edan + Melissa Shoshahi
events.note: Two headliners rather than a showcase, which is the right shape for a Tuesday. Drink minimum on top of the ticket.

events.title: Gilla Band with Annie-Claude Deschênes
events.note: The Dublin band formerly called Girl Band — guitar noise built like industrial machinery with Dara Kiely talking himself into a corner over it. Deschênes, late of Duchess Says, opens, which makes this the best-matched bill of the week.

events.title: Rebecca Black with bayli
events.note: The Exhibitionism tour: hyperpop that is genuinely good and entirely aware of the joke it spent a decade outrunning. Sold out. Doors seven.

events.title: Chronovisor
events.note: A title in the Roxie's current run; descriptor withheld rather than guessed.

events.title: MISSIO with Fifteenoeight and Kent Osborne
events.note: Austin electro-rock, heavier live than on record, on the Love & Heartbreak tour. All ages.

events.title: Blade Runner: The Final Cut (35mm)
events.note: On a print, which is the only way the rain and the smoke read properly. Scott's own cut, no voiceover, no happy ending.

events.title: Kilowatt Karaoke
events.note: Mission karaoke with no stage and no sign-up sheet to speak of. Free.

events.title: Live Model Tuesday Sketch
events.note: Life drawing in a bar, which works better than it sounds. Bring paper; nobody minds what you produce.

events.title: Madrone Karaoke
events.note: The Tuesday karaoke that follows the sketch night, in the same room, with the same lighting.

events.title: Olivia O'Brien with Sophie Cates
events.note: Post-SoundCloud pop with the sadness left in rather than produced out. August Hall publishes no times on its calendar.

events.title: Sobs with Lace
events.note: Singaporean indie pop with the jangle turned up and the melancholy underneath — closer to 1990s Sarah Records than to anything current. No time published.

events.title: Taylor Bickett with Fairhazel
events.note: Plain-spoken confessional songwriting in the oldest saloon in the city. Time not published on the sweep.

events.title: The Illusion of Space: Patrick Hughes
events.note: Penultimate day of the reverspective show on Geary.

events.title: Dirk Powell and Amelia Powell
events.note: Appalachian fiddle and banjo played as living repertoire rather than preservation, father and daughter, in a seated listening room. Time follows the Freight's standard weeknight curtain.

events.title: Gully Boys, Pollyanna and For Horses
events.note: Minneapolis pop-punk trio at the volunteer-run all-ages institution, five dollars. The regional sweep files this show at Cornerstone; Gilman's own ticketing page has it, so this is where it is.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Bess Wohl's Pulitzer winner — a daughter restaging her mother's 1970s consciousness-raising group in the basketball court where it met. The West Coast premiere, and the best-reviewed new play in the country this year.

events.title: Mezcal & Mole Comedy Night
events.note: The Tuesday half of Mesa Maguey's comedy week, free with RSVP.

events.title: First Tuesdays Free Comedy Showcase
events.note: Downtown Oakland's first-Tuesday showcase, free with RSVP, happy hour running alongside it.

events.title: The Spyrals, Alex E.T. and UFO Baby
events.note: San Francisco psych-garage at the top of a three-band local bill. The Spyrals have been doing this longer than most of the rooms they play have existed.

events.title: Vote Yes on Measure Y — For Berkeley Arts
events.note: An election-night rally for the Berkeley arts measure, in a theatre the measure would fund. Doors seven.

events.title: Lee Ritenour
events.note: Second of two nights. Same catalogue, looser band by the end of a run.

events.title: XG
events.note: The Japanese group who record in English and dance like a hip-hop crew rather than a pop group. An arena booking, listed for completeness.

events.title: Shrek the Musical Jr.
events.note: Campbell Union School District's production in the 800-seat Heritage. Listed as multiple dates with only the Thursday visible on the venue's page.

events.title: PX Floro
events.note: A Wednesday headline slot at the Improv, which is where the touring circuit tests the South Bay.

events.title: Roosters Comedy Showcase
events.note: The club's own midweek showcase — four or five comics working out material. Two-item minimum.

events.title: Taste of Filoli Tour
events.note: Ninety minutes through the kitchen gardens and the orchard with the produce at the end of it.

events.title: Henry Diltz: Behind the Lens
events.note: The photographer who shot the Doors, CSN and Woodstock, narrating his own contact sheets. Doors seven. He does the same evening at Sweetwater the next night.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The Wednesday free hour. Same rule, emptier garden than the weekend.

events.title: San Francisco Zoo Free Admission Day
events.note: Free for San Francisco residents with ID, capacity permitting — the November resident day. Go at opening; the queue is the whole risk.

events.title: Free Admission Day at Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: YBCA's galleries are free every Wednesday — Dread Scott's The Body Politic, Rael San Fratello's Prototypes and Provocations and GaHee Park upstairs. The Dread Scott is the one to make time for.

events.title: GLBT History Museum Free First Wednesday
events.note: The first museum of its kind in the United States, free on the first Wednesday, first-come-first-served. Harvey Milk's kitchen table is in there.

events.title: Valkyries Championship Parade
events.note: The Valkyries won the title in their second season and the city is closing the Embarcadero for it. Free, outdoors, and the first championship parade a San Francisco women's team has ever had. Get north of the Ferry Building early; the Muni surface lines will not cope.

events.title: Free Art Workshop: Clay Tile Textures
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Two hours of hand-building in the Grand Lobby on the free day. Registration required and it fills.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Wednesday matinee. The physical comedy reads better with a daylight audience than it has any right to.

events.title: Gallery Tour and Sketching: Dread Scott and Rael San Fratello
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: A led walk through both ground-floor shows with drawing time built in. Free with registration.

events.title: Mahjong and Martinis at The Jay
events.note: Tile games in a Jackson Square hotel bar, half five to half seven. More sociable than competitive; the price is whatever you drink.

events.title: Union Square Ice Rink Opening Ceremony
events.note: The rink opens for the season and the first hundred skaters in the 5.30 and 7pm sessions go free; after that it is $22 with skates. Outdoors, in Union Square, which is the point.

events.title: An Evening with Jane Schoenbrun: Public Access Afterworld + I Saw the TV Glow
events.note: Schoenbrun in person with the new work and the film that made her name. Co-presented with Book Passage, and the most oversubscribed screening in the city this week.

events.title: How SF Neo-Futurists Run 100 Shows a Year
events.note: The company behind The Infinite Wrench explaining the machinery: thirty plays in sixty minutes, re-written weekly, for eleven years. Free, Steve Silver Room, fourth floor.

events.title: Runa Simi
events.note: A documentary on dubbing Hollywood into Quechua, with the director, the protagonist and the producer in the room afterwards.

events.title: Drink and Draw Art Event and Raffle
events.note: Free drawing night at the Knockout with a raffle at the end — one of the two Knockout nights the ticketing calendar does not carry.

events.title: South Side Beer Ride
events.note: A free monthly shuttle between the Bayview and Dogpatch breweries. The bus costs nothing; everything else does.

events.title: Landroid, Fake Your Own Death and Misandrist
events.note: Three local bands and no touring act, which on a Wednesday is a recommendation rather than a complaint.

events.title: Pain of Truth with Killing Time, Missing Link, Mizery and Eternal Form
events.note: Five hardcore bands in a gilded 1907 hall, with Killing Time — New York Hardcore's actual first generation — second on the bill. Doors six.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Wednesday evening, the second of two performances that day.

events.title: Ryli
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: A performance in Gallery 3 on the free Wednesday, starting promptly at seven. Free with RSVP and the capacity is a gallery's, not a hall's.

events.title: Team Dresch with The Third Sex and Longstocking
events.note: The queercore record that mattered most, played by the band that made it, with two of their contemporaries — in a room that closes for good at the end of 2026. Two nights; this is the first and the one to take. Doors seven.

events.title: Free Comedy Night
events.note: The Wednesday edition. Free with RSVP, $20–$25 at the door, two-drink minimum.

events.title: SFDanceworks Season 9
events.note: Four nights on the Steindler Stage from a company that commissions rather than revives. $36, and the discount code SFDW9 was still live when this was compiled.

events.title: Blue Light with Sassy 009, Swordes and Tricky FM
events.note: Sassy 009 — Norwegian electronic pop built out of flute, pitched vocals and bass that arrives late — on a four-act club bill. All ages.

events.title: INOHA with Buddha Trixie and Flight By Nothing
events.note: Hazy guitar pop at the top of a three-band bill, with San Diego's Buddha Trixie in the middle slot doing the heavier version of the same idea.

events.title: Psyched! Fest 2026: Shifters, The Intelligence and Dizz Brew
events.note: The Knockout's night of the city-wide psych festival that runs to the 6th. The Intelligence have been making lopsided garage records for twenty years and have never made a boring one.

events.title: The History of Concrete
events.note: The late show, after the Schoenbrun evening.

events.title: Mary in the Junkyard with Lefty Parker
events.note: A London trio who play quietly until they do not — cello, drums and a voice that sounds unbothered right up to the point it breaks. Doors eight.

events.title: Wild at Heart (4K restoration)
events.note: Nine o'clock, the night after costume night.

events.title: South Taurids Meteor Shower Peaks
events.note: The Taurids are slow and sparse but throw more fireballs than any other shower of the year. Peak overnight; get away from the city lights and look south-east.

events.title: Big Brain: Engineering Telekinesis — Brain-Computer Interfaces
events.note: A neuroscientist on restoring movement with implanted electrodes, in a bar, for free. The Big Brain series is the best science talk in the city that does not require a lanyard.

events.title: DICE with The Back Alley
events.note: Downstairs at the du Nord, where the booking is usually better than the billing. No time published.

events.title: Greenhouse
events.note: Live music in a repertory cinema in the Richmond, which is most of what the room does on a weeknight. No time on the mirror.

events.title: Local/Global with DJ maDRE
events.note: Afrobeat, highlife and the Caribbean end of it, selected rather than mixed. Free.

events.title: Patch Bay: Translating Living Systems into Robotics and Music
events.note: Scott Kildall and Kal Spelletich on making machines out of biological behaviour, in the one room in the city that programmes this as a matter of course. No time published.

events.title: Harun Farocki's War at a Distance and Videos by Mahmoud Alhaj
events.note: Farocki on how industrial and military images are made and read, paired with new Palestinian video work. The most argued-about programme BAMPFA has run this autumn.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Second of six performances this week.

events.title: Ms. Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean with DJ D Sharp
events.note: Thirty years of The Score, two of the three Fugees, outdoors in the Greek in November — which is a gamble on the weather and still the biggest booking of the week. Doors half five. Bring layers; the hill gets cold the moment the sun goes.

events.title: Hometown Free Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP in Emeryville, happy hour running through it.

events.title: Cherronda G: I'm Every Woman
events.note: A Chaka Khan songbook night from a Bay Area vocalist who can actually carry it. Seated.

events.title: Secret Family, Richard Tripps and Brown Dog
events.note: The same three-band bill that plays Santa Cruz the night before, in the better room.

events.title: How the 2020 Census Was Made: Danah Boyd
events.note: Boyd on the differential-privacy fight inside the 2020 census — the most consequential statistics argument of the decade, free, in Mountain View. The listing names no room.

events.title: Don Omar
events.note: The Last King tour. Reggaetón's second-generation architect in an arena, listed for completeness.

events.title: Helen Hong
events.note: First of four nights in Sunnyvale, with Gary Michael Anderson and Angel Castro. Two-item minimum.

events.title: Jack Assadourian Jr.
events.note: A Thursday headline at the Improv.

events.title: Raphaël Feuillâtre: Latin Passions
events.note: A classical guitarist who won the GFA at twenty-two and plays Baroque transcriptions as though they were written for the instrument. Bing's acoustic is built for exactly this.

events.title: Free First Thursday at the Museum of Craft and Design
events.note: The Dogpatch's small, consistently good design museum, free on the first Thursday.

events.title: The History of Concrete
events.note: A half-three matinee.

events.title: Downtown First Thursdays with Big Freedia
events.note: The monthly downtown block party, and this month it has Big Freedia on it — New Orleans bounce in the middle of Second Street, free with RSVP, five till ten. The best free music in the city this week by a distance.

events.title: Opening Reception: From Street to Stage with Beaver Bauer
events.note: Fifty years of costume design for the Pickle Family Circus, Teatro ZinZanni and A.C.T., in the Jewett Gallery. Bauer is one of the great Bay Area theatre-makers and almost nobody knows her name.

events.title: Market Street Pack Walk
events.note: A dog walk organised as a civic act, down the middle of Market. Free, and funnier than it sounds.

events.title: 30th Arab Film Festival: Opening Night
events.note: Ten days, forty films, twenty-six countries, thirtieth year — the longest-running festival of its kind in the country opens in Japantown. $45 for opening night, $20 a ticket after.

events.title: Fjord
events.note: Early evening.

events.title: Live Latin Jazz: Pepe and Friends
events.note: Three hours of Latin jazz in a Jackson Square hotel bar, no cover.

events.title: Lower Polk / Tenderloin Art Walk
events.note: Trendyloin's monthly walk through the galleries and storefronts on and off Polk. Free, and the art is more interesting than the Union Square circuit.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Also screening at New People this week.

events.title: SF State Rooftop Stargazing
events.note: The university opens its roof and its large telescope to anybody who turns up, free, weather permitting. In November the weather is the whole question.

events.title: Flight Club: Adult Flight Night
events.note: Trampolines in a Presidio hangar, 18+, $20 an hour, grip socks compulsory.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Thursday evening.

events.title: New People: Paprika
events.note: Satoshi Kon's dream-invasion film, programmed by the Roxie into the Japantown screen. The second show is at 9.20.

events.title: Free HellaFunny Thursday Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP, $20–$25 at the door, two-drink minimum.

events.title: SFDanceworks Season 9
events.note: Second of four nights on the Steindler Stage.

events.title: The Rape of Mrs. Brown
events.note: Maurya Kerr's tinypistol in a work whose title is doing deliberate violence to the audience before the curtain. The strongest thing in Mission dance this week.

events.title: AZ Chike
events.note: Compton rap at double speed over beats that barely hold still. Sold out. All ages.

events.title: Danny L Harle with Ms* Gloom
events.note: The PC Music producer behind half of hyperpop's grammar, playing the hard-dance end of his own catalogue. Doors seven.

events.title: Greg Freeman with Trinity Ace
events.note: Vermont songwriting with the guitars left ragged — the record everybody who writes about this stuff spent the spring on.

events.title: Marci with the booyah! kids
events.note: Montreal synth-pop that sounds like 1984 and knows it. A 150-cap bar is the wrong size for it, which is why it is worth going.

events.title: Mystery Skulls and Fox Stevenson
events.note: Electro-funk and drum and bass sharing a bill in a 1931 nightclub with the original fittings. Doors seven, 21+.

events.title: Squirrel Flower with Sour Widows
events.note: Ella Williams writes about weather and damage in the same breath and plays loud enough to mean it. Oakland's Sour Widows open, which makes this the best-paired bill in the city tonight. Doors seven, all ages.

events.title: Lady
events.note: The late slot.

events.title: 16th & Mission Open Mic
events.note: No microphone, no stage, no permission. The open mic on the BART plaza is the most reliably strange hour in the city.

events.title: Alien
events.note: Nine o'clock, on the Roxie's screen, with an audience that knows every beat and still jumps.

events.title: Crazy Karaoke
events.note: Karaoke until two with $3 shots. Free with RSVP, 21+.

events.title: Inner Circle Dance Party
events.note: Free with RSVP every Thursday.

events.title: Level Up Thursdays: Free Video DJ Dance Party
events.note: Video DJing on Folsom until two, free, every Thursday.

events.title: She's in Parties: 1980s Post-Punk and New Wave Dance Party
events.note: Goth, post-punk and electro on the Knockout's floor until late. The longest-running night of its kind in the Mission.

events.title: Sadderday: Emo, Pop-Punk and Screamo Dance Party
events.note: A free emo night; the listing names no room, which is how it is posted.

events.title: Brazilian Disco
events.note: Brazilian boogie and disco edits, free, which is the Madrone's standing bargain.

events.title: Brazilian Wax
events.note: The second Thursday room at the Madrone, same country, heavier on the samba-soul end.

events.title: Dave Hause & The Mermaid with Darius Koski
events.note: Philadelphia heartland punk gone acoustic-ish, with Swingin' Utters' Darius Koski opening. No time published on the calendar.

events.title: Function 500 with FLUXIONS
events.note: Local 500's night in the Public Works loft. The venue publishes no times on its calendar.

events.title: Moby with Azzecca and DJ Holographic
events.note: A DJ set rather than a live show, in a 7,000-capacity civic hall. Three minutes from BART Civic Center, which matters more than the $45 garage.

events.title: Free First Thursday at BAMPFA
events.note: Galleries free on the first Thursday; film programmes are still charged. Maren Hassinger's Living Moving Growing is the reason to come.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: A one o'clock matinee, which is the easiest Liberation to get into this week.

events.title: Curator's Tour: Maren Hassinger, Living Moving Growing
events.note: Anthony Graham through the Hassinger survey on the free day — fifty years of wire rope, branches and bodies. Forty-five minutes and it changes how the room reads.

events.title: Wrenching News Workshops
events.note: A making workshop built around the news cycle, free on the first Thursday.

events.title: POC Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP in Temescal.

events.title: Solas
events.note: Thirty years of the best Irish-American band of their generation — Seamus Egan and Winifred Horan with Moira Smiley singing. They play Montalvo the next night; this is the better room.

events.title: The Secret
events.note: A Thursday-night screening in BAMPFA's barrel theatre, which has the best projection in the East Bay.

events.title: Córdoba
events.note: Flamenco-inflected jazz in a seated room.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Thursday evening, the second performance of the day.

events.title: Non Plus Temps, Pateka, Murder Murder and Joseph Dee Bradshow
events.note: An album release at the top of a four-band Oakland bill. Non Plus Temps make the angular, dubbed-out post-punk that Oakland has quietly been best at for a decade.

events.title: Colleen Green
events.note: Fuzz-pop songs about doing nothing, delivered over a drum machine, in a 150-cap room. One of four Ivy Room nights this week.

events.title: Shwayze with Asher Roth and Chiddy Bang
events.note: A late-2000s rap bill, nostalgic in the honest way. Carried by the regional sweep and absent from Cornerstone's own page — see the reachability notes.

events.title: Good Vibez San Jose: Rebelution, Waka Flocka Flame and Collie Buddz
events.note: A rescheduled September festival landing in November: California reggae-rock, Jamaican dancehall and Atlanta rap on one outdoor bill in East San Jose. The largest ticketed event in the South Bay this week.

events.title: South First Fridays Art Walk
events.note: San Jose's monthly art walk through the SoFA galleries and the museums around them, free. The best free evening in the South Bay this month.

events.title: San Jose Barracuda vs Bakersfield Condors
events.note: AHL hockey next door to SAP Center, first of two nights against the same opponent. Cheap, fast and nobody tells you to sit down.

events.title: Mark Normand
events.note: Four shows across Friday and Saturday, almost sold out when this was compiled. The second Friday show is at 9.45.

events.title: Solas
events.note: The Saratoga date, with Moira Smiley, Winifred Horan, Seamus Egan and Alan G. Murray. The Carriage House is 300 seats under the trees and the ticket link adds an $8 fee.

events.title: Helen Hong
events.note: Second of four Sunnyvale nights.

events.title: Mon Laferte with Silvana Estrada
events.note: The Femme Fatale tour. Laferte writes boleros, cumbia and rock in the same set and means all of it; Silvana Estrada opening makes this the strongest Spanish-language bill of the week. An arena, so never featured — but the music deserves better than the room.

events.title: Rock en Español Night
events.note: A DJ night of Soda Stereo through Zoé in a 500-cap room. The cheap counterpart to the SAP Center bill an hour earlier.

events.title: DubVision
events.note: Dutch progressive house, Sunnyvale, 21+. Six minutes' walk from Caltrain Sunnyvale and the street parking is free after six.

events.title: Dan and Phil
events.note: Dan Howell and Phil Lester's live tour, in a 3,000-seat hall. Carried by the regional sweep only; the JamBase mirror this file uses for the Civic does not have it and publishes no time.

events.title: History Museum Free First Friday
events.note: Free all day on the first Friday, in the 1910 county courthouse — the dome alone is worth the Caltrain.

events.title: Zoppé Italian Family Circus
events.note: A one-ring Italian circus under canvas in Redwood City, to 29 November. $12–$37 by age and seat; the clown is the fifth generation of the same family.

events.title: The Addams Family
events.note: Palo Alto Players in the musical, Friday curtain half seven. Running to 15 November.

events.title: Peter Antoniou: Pretty Psychic
events.note: Mentalism played for laughs rather than awe, which is the only honest way to do it. Doors seven, show eight.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The Friday free hour, nine to ten.

events.title: Pay-What-You-Can Taco Day
events.note: Pay between nothing and ten dollars, Bayview, Third Street. A standing Friday and a genuinely good taco.

events.title: Jam Session with Creativity Explored
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: The Mission studio for artists with developmental disabilities takes over YBCA's Front Door Gallery for ninety minutes. Free with RSVP.

events.title: Dirtybird Night Market
events.note: Claude VonStroke's label doing a free DJ night with food stalls on the plaza outside Chase Center. Free, outdoors, and the Muni T drops you at the door.

events.title: North Beach First Fridays Art Crawl
events.note: Galleries and storefronts open late across North Beach, free. Smaller and better-tempered than the Oakland walk.

events.title: Ocean Beach: 24 Bay Area Photographers
events.note: Two dozen photographers on one four-mile beach, in the city's municipal darkroom. Free.

events.title: ZooLights
events.note: The zoo's winter light season opens and runs to 3 January. $30 on a separate evening ticket, and the fog does half the work.

events.title: Movies at Mechanics'
events.note: The Friday film at 57 Post Street, in a library founded in 1854. Downtown SF carries the time but not the title; the institute's own listing sits past where a plain fetch stops.

events.title: New People: Being Heumann
events.note: Judy Heumann's life and the disability-rights movement she built, open-captioned, with a Q&A in the room.

events.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
events.note: A new title opening the Roxie's weekend; descriptor withheld rather than guessed.

events.title: Fatherland
events.note: A new documentary in the weekend run; descriptor withheld rather than guessed.

events.title: Dylan Thom and Horse Laugh
events.note: An early local double bill before the Kilowatt's late show.

events.title: Floating Features: Pacific Heights
events.note: A San Francisco-set thriller in a San Francisco cinema, which is the whole appeal of the Floating Features series.

events.title: Golden Gate Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP, 21+.

events.title: HellaSecret Crazy Funny Asians
events.note: Two shows, seven and nine, free with RSVP, $5–$10 donation suggested. Location on booking.

events.title: Rush Hour Comedy Night
events.note: The earlier of the Function's two Friday bills, free with RSVP.

events.title: Steven Universe in Concert
events.note: Rebecca Sugar's songs with an ensemble, under the vaults on Nob Hill. An odd fit that works — the cathedral's reverb suits music written to be sung by children.

events.title: Janet Thornburg's Cognitive Divine
events.note: A solo piece; the listing names no room.

events.title: SF Symphony: Isabel Leonard Sings Ravel
events.note: Fabien Gabel conducts d'Indy's Istar, Ravel's Shéhérazade and Debussy's Le jet d'eau with Isabel Leonard, then Strauss's Symphonic Fantasy on Die Frau ohne Schatten — the Debussy and the Strauss are both first performances by this orchestra. Recovered from sfsymphony.org's own ticket page, which answered this run even though its calendar still does not.

events.title: SFDanceworks Season 9
events.note: Third of four nights.

events.title: Taylor Mac in Concert
events.note: Mac solo, a week after the Glass and Ginsberg programme at Stanford — judy's cabaret voice with a 1,600-seat house to fill and no chorus to hide behind. The Curran's own site answered this run with a 503, so this comes from the venue's ticketing agent.

events.title: Buena Vista Orchestra
events.note: The surviving Buena Vista Social Club lineage, playing son and danzón in a 2,300-seat theatre, as part of the week's psych festival's wider programme.

events.title: Joshua Redman
events.note: Thirty years in and still the most melodically patient tenor of his generation. SFJAZZ's main hall, which is the only room in the city built for this. Time follows the hall's standard curtain; the mirror this run uses publishes none.

events.title: Loquat (10-year reunion), Halou and Steilacoom
events.note: A San Francisco electronic-pop reunion with the two bands it shared a scene with, in the room they all played. Doors eight.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Friday evening.

events.title: SYML
events.note: Brian Fennell solo in the Castro, which is a lot of room for one piano and a voice — and exactly the right amount. Doors seven.

events.title: San Francisco Bike Party
events.note: First Friday, meet-up announced the week of the ride, free, and about a thousand people on bicycles with sound systems.

events.title: San Francisco Leonard Cohen Festival
events.note: Two nights of Cohen upstairs at the du Nord, in a 1907 Swedish fraternal hall with the woodwork intact. First night.

events.title: The Stoner Comedy Jam
events.note: Free with RSVP in a consumption lounge, one-item minimum, 21+.

events.title: Ken Russell's The Devils (4K restoration)
events.note: The film the studio cut to pieces and the Catholic Church tried to bury, restored. Still the most unhinged thing Oliver Reed ever did.

events.title: Clay Street Unit with Maxwell Oaks
events.note: Jam-adjacent funk at nine. All ages.

events.title: Funktion: A Freestyle and Beats Dance Party
events.note: The Freakstyle Posse playing freestyle and electro-funk, which in the Mission means people who actually remember it.

events.title: Genesis Owusu with After Louise and Aaron Axelsen
events.note: Ghanaian-Australian, and the only artist working who can put funk, hardcore and rap in the same four minutes without it sounding like a compromise. Doors eight. Comfortably the best ticket in the city under $35 tonight.

events.title: King Buffalo with L.A. Witch
events.note: Rochester heavy psych — long, patient, enormously loud — with L.A. Witch's reverb-soaked garage underneath it. The loudest good show of the week.

events.title: The Infinite Wrench
events.note: Thirty plays in sixty minutes, re-shuffled weekly, with a dice roll at the door deciding part of the price. Eleven years in and still the most reliably alive hour of theatre in the city.

events.title: Your Fucked Up Relationship
events.note: Improv built from audience confessions about their own relationships. Mission, 21+.

events.title: Honey Channel with Miel Beton, Hard Shiny Plastic and Bstone
events.note: The ten o'clock bill, four acts deep, which is the Kilowatt's real Friday.

events.title: The Ritual
events.note: The late improv slot, cheaper and stranger than the earlier one.

events.title: 2026 World Deaf & Disabled Dance Film Festival
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Two days in YBCA's screening room. $28.52 a ticket, $87.21 for the Saturday pass; the page publishes no times.

events.title: Adriatique
events.note: Swiss melodic-techno duo in the Dogpatch warehouse. No time published.

events.title: Bahamas
events.note: Afie Jurvanen's soft-edged guitar songs, on the Industrial Sport & Sound tour.

events.title: Baukunst First Fridays: Art, Music and Food
events.note: A first-Friday opening in Bernal Heights. The listing gives no start time.

events.title: Ben Wolfe with Joel Ross, Nicole Glover and Aaron Kimmel
events.note: A bassist's quartet with Joel Ross on vibes in the 100-seat Lab — the better jazz ticket in the building tonight if you want to hear the instruments. Found on the Songkick mirror; the JamBase one does not carry it.

events.title: Block Fest: Tenderloin Arts Festival
events.note: A free Tenderloin arts festival with open art-making. RSVP required and the page gives no start time.

events.title: Bounce SF: Ueberrest, Flash Gea and dj try
events.note: Part of a two-night festival at Public Works. Times unpublished.

events.title: Fort Mason Night Market
events.note: The monthly night market on the Fort Mason pier. Free to enter; no time published on the campus calendar.

events.title: IAN SWEET with Luella
events.note: Jilian Medford's project — guitar pop that keeps undercutting its own hooks. Downstairs. No time published.

events.title: Lucy Bedroque with pinponpanpon
events.note: First of two Regency nights. No time published on the mirror.

events.title: Mira, yaego and Main Phase
events.note: Three rooms at 1015 on a Friday; the venue's own site fetches empty, so this is the regional sweep's account of it.

events.title: Snot with Bleeding Through, Breaking In A Sequence and Saltwound
events.note: Late-1990s Santa Barbara nu-metal with Orange County metalcore under it. Both mirrors agree on this one show; DNA's own calendar refuses this run, so its club and film nights are missing from the week.

events.title: Thee Sinseers with The Charities
events.note: East LA sweet soul, played straight — no irony, no retro wink, just the Arlen Sinseer songbook. No time on the mirror.

events.title: fieldtest: DJ Koolt and Naone
events.note: The loft half of the same night.

events.title: Mean Streets
events.note: Scorsese's third film, and the one where the method arrives all at once. Four o'clock.

events.title: Oakland First Fridays
events.note: Twenty blocks of Telegraph closed, free, five till half nine. The largest free monthly street event in the Bay Area and the week's best argument for BART.

events.title: Pleasant Hill Night Market
events.note: Free night market with food and performances. Filed to the East Bay by proximity; Pleasant Hill is not a city the brief names.

events.title: Mini Masterpieces Holiday Gifts Show
events.note: Small work priced to be bought, in Alameda's arts centre. Free with RSVP.

events.title: Oakland Art Murmur
events.note: The galleries' own first-Friday walk, which predates the street festival around it and is still the better art.

events.title: Oakland Diwali Festival of Light
events.note: Free Diwali celebration in downtown Oakland.

events.title: Harakiri
events.note: Kobayashi's 1962 demolition of the samurai code — the best-composed film in BAMPFA's Kobayashi run, which continues on Saturday and Sunday.

events.title: HellaSecret Speakeasy Comedy
events.note: Free on limited tickets with a code, otherwise discounted. Location on booking.

events.title: Lalo Guerrero Legacy Festival
events.note: The father of Chicano music, celebrated by his son Mark Guerrero with La Doña and Dr. Loco's Rockin' Jalapeño Band. Two nights. Guerrero wrote pachuco boogie, Mexican swing and protest corridos across sixty years and almost nobody outside Los Angeles programmes him; this is the most historically serious booking in the Bay Area this week.

events.title: Plini with Portraits and Night Verses
events.note: Australian instrumental prog-metal, technically absurd and more melodic than the genre usually allows. Doors six.

events.title: Jessie Reyez with Adria Kain
events.note: Toronto R&B with the rasp left in. Sold out. Doors seven.

events.title: Oakland Critical Mass
events.note: First Friday, meet at the plaza, free.

events.title: Queer Club Classics with DJ Louie El Ser
events.note: Five dollars, Oakland, late.

events.title: Andre Nickatina
events.note: The Fillmore rapper in a 150-capacity room in Albany, which is an absurd and excellent mismatch.

events.title: Covenant
events.note: York Walker's Delta folk-horror about a bluesman who comes home too rich too fast. First previews this week; press night is 11 November. Berkeley Rep's own site answers this run with a redirect loop, so no curtain time could be confirmed.

events.title: Dwele
events.note: Detroit neo-soul, seated, in a 400-seat room.

events.title: Y&T
events.note: Oakland's own hard-rock survivors, forty-plus years in. Carried by the regional sweep and absent from Cornerstone's own page.

events.title: San José Roots Cultural Fest and Historic Home Tours
events.note: Free, in and around the oldest built fabric in the city, with the Peralta Adobe open. The best free thing in the South Bay this weekend.

events.title: San Jose State Spartans vs Northern Illinois Huskies
events.note: College football on a Saturday afternoon, cheap and walkable from downtown.

events.title: Total Vibez Live: Keyshia Cole and Ashanti
events.note: The second outdoor festival at Lake Cunningham in two days — 2000s R&B this time, in the open air in East San Jose.

events.title: Back 2 the Bay with Keak Da Sneak
events.note: Hyphy's own, early doors, before the house night takes the room.

events.title: Earlybirds Club 80s Party
events.note: An early-evening dance party that finishes before most clubs open — a format that deserves to spread.

events.title: San Jose Barracuda vs Bakersfield Condors
events.note: Second of two against Bakersfield.

events.title: Dan + Shay with Tyler Hubbard and Josh Ross
events.note: An outdoor shed booking in November, which is unusual enough to flag: both the JamBase mirror and the South Bay feed carry it, but Shoreline's season normally closes in October. Dress for a cold lawn. $40 to park, or ride the bike path.

events.title: Helen Hong
events.note: Third of four nights, seven o'clock.

events.title: Mark Normand
events.note: Two Saturday shows, seven and half nine.

events.title: Santa Clara Broncos vs Sacramento State Hornets
events.note: Third Broncos home game of the week.

events.title: Songs of the Fall
events.note: The Symphony San Jose Chorale and players, Elena Sharkova conducting Whitacre, Argento, Persichetti and Lauridsen in the 1926 mission church. An hour, no interval, $25 for students and $45 in advance — the best-value serious music in the South Bay this week.

events.title: Álvaro Díaz
events.note: Puerto Rican rap and reggaetón with more melancholy in it than the genre usually permits, in a 3,000-seat hall.

events.title: Audien
events.note: Progressive house, Sunnyvale, 21+.

events.title: Discover Taiwan Expo
events.note: Two days of Taiwanese food, crafts and performance in the Expo Hall, $3.79 general admission. A convention centre, so deprioritised — but at under four dollars it earns the line.

events.title: History in Motion Grand Opening
events.note: A new permanent gallery opening free to the public in the old courthouse.

events.title: Taste of Filoli Tour
events.note: The Saturday garden-and-produce walk.

events.title: The Addams Family
events.note: Saturday matinee, ASL-interpreted.

events.title: Zoppé Italian Family Circus
events.note: The Saturday performance under canvas.

events.title: Yasmin Williams
events.note: Fingerstyle guitar played across the lap, with a kalimba taped to the body of the instrument — and none of it is a gimmick. Two shows, seven and nine, in a room that seats a couple of hundred. The best Peninsula booking of the week.

events.title: The Addams Family
events.note: Saturday evening.

events.title: Noe Valley Farmers Market
events.note: Saturdays, eight till one, on the square the neighbourhood fought for.

events.title: Free Legion of Honor Day for Bay Area Residents
events.note: Same rule, same group, better view.

events.title: Free de Young Museum Day for Bay Area Residents
events.venue: de Young Museum, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Every Saturday, free to Bay Area residents with ID, timed tickets required. The second free day at the de Young this week.

events.title: Bank of America Museums on Us
events.note: First full weekend of the month: free admission at the de Young, the Legion, OMCA, the Contemporary Jewish Museum and others for Bank of America and Merrill cardholders. Worth knowing if you hold the card and nothing if you do not.

events.title: Día de los Muertos and Diwali at the Presidio
events.note: Two festivals of light and the dead on the same afternoon at Crissy Field, with a fire ceremony. Free, outdoors, with the bridge behind it.

events.title: San Francisco Coffee Festival
events.note: Tenth year, two days, tastings and live music in the Festival Pavilion. From $29, and the 9.30 session is the one where you can still taste anything.

events.title: District 2 Marina Family Summit
events.note: A neighbourhood civic day with food and childcare provided, free.

events.title: San Francisco Fall Cider Fest
events.note: Unlimited tastings from thirty-plus cider makers in Mission Bay, 21+, from $45.

events.title: Las Almas ni los Ojos
events.note: Part of Colombia on Film, presented by CiNEOLA with RoxCine. One o'clock.

events.title: Manilatown Film Double Feature
events.note: Two Filipino-American films on the I-Hotel and the neighbourhood the city demolished around it, with Q&As. Free or donation, RSVP required.

events.title: Palina and The Cave, Electric Ex and Your Stray Dog
events.note: An afternoon three-band local bill; the ticketing calendar carries it twice under two links, so it is one show.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Saturday matinee.

events.title: Wood Street: Oakland's Unhoused
events.note: A documentary on the Wood Street encampment and its eviction, with a Q&A. Free, no RSVP, first come at the door.

events.title: New People: My Undesirable Friends, Part 2 — Exile (Chapters 4–5)
events.note: Julia Loktev's long record of independent Russian journalists leaving, with one of the protagonists present. Four hours of the most important documentary work being made anywhere.

events.title: SFDanceworks Community Workshop with Isaac Bates-Vinueza
events.note: Two hours of open class with one of the company's dancers, registration required.

events.title: SF Symphony: Día de los Muertos
events.note: The nineteenth annual: José Luis Gómez conducts Chávez, Moncayo and Márquez, Francisco Fullana plays the Fandango, and Luis Farfán Carrillo's El Baile de la Catrina for two salterios and orchestra gets its world premiere, danced by Casa Círculo Cultural. Free catrinas and altars in the lobby beforehand. Three in the afternoon, and the most interesting programme the orchestra will play this month.

events.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
events.note: Saturday afternoon.

events.title: The Dalai Lama: My Religion Is Kindness
events.note: With the director and a guest in the room.

events.title: Matinee Show: Trash Vampires, Crop Top, Don't Ask and Golfball Jr.
events.note: Four bands at five in the afternoon, which is the civilised way to see a punk bill.

events.title: Flamenco Nights at El Lopo
events.note: Flamenco in a Polk Street bar, $25, two-item minimum, 21+. The room is far too small and that is why it works.

events.title: Fatherland
events.note: Saturday early evening.

events.title: Free Book Reading: A Childhood on the Hippie Trail
events.note: A memoir of being driven overland to India as a child, read in the best second-hand bookshop in the Mission. Free.

events.title: Free Night Walking Tour: Chinatown Alleyways and North Beach
events.note: Tip-based, starts at the Dragon Gate, and the alleyways are the point — Ross, Spofford, Cameron, after dark.

events.title: Last Supper Party: Poetry, Music and Community Bread
events.note: Poetry, music and a shared loaf in a Mission bar. Free with RSVP.

events.title: New People: Being Heumann
events.note: The second open-captioned screening with a Q&A.

events.title: Crazy Funny Asians
events.note: Free with RSVP, $5–$10 donation suggested, $25 at the door.

events.title: Golden Gate Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP, 21+.

events.title: Shoplifters United and Debased
events.note: A Smiths tribute and a Pixies tribute on one bill — real fixtures of the free-and-cheap circuit, and never the thing to feature over an original act.

events.title: SFDanceworks Season 9
events.note: Closing night of four.

events.title: The Marriage of Figaro
events.note: Third of nine. Four hours, and the Act III finale is the reason opera exists.

events.title: Fjord
events.note: Saturday night.

events.title: PJ Morton
events.note: Maroon 5's keyboard player and a far better artist in his own name — gospel-rooted soul, played live rather than programmed. Doors seven. The regional sweep files this at a theatre in Castro Valley; the Castro's own calendar has it, so this is where it is.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Saturday evening.

events.title: Puff Puff Laugh
events.note: Free with RSVP in a consumption lounge, one-item minimum, 21+.

events.title: San Francisco Leonard Cohen Festival: Conspiracy of Beards, Daniel Kahn and Jake Shulman-Ment
events.note: Thirty men singing Cohen a cappella, plus Yiddish song from Daniel Kahn and Jake Shulman-Ment's fiddle. Night two, and the strangest good thing in the city tonight.

events.title: Southern Culture on the Skids with Van Goat
events.note: The better of their two Bay Area nights, in a room that closes at the end of the year. Doors seven, 21+.

events.title: The Confessional
events.note: Improv from audience sins and secrets.

events.title: The Secret Museum
events.note: A premiere about the Pompeii frescoes kept from public view for two centuries. $30; the listing names no cinema.

events.title: Alex Cameron with Josh da Costa
events.note: Character-driven Australian songwriting in which the narrator is always slightly worse than you hoped. Doors eight, all ages.

events.title: Brüxie & Friends: Ghetto Tech House Night
events.note: Free with RSVP; the listing names no room.

events.title: HellaSecret Desi Comedy Night
events.note: Free for the first hundred RSVPs, $25 at the door. Two shows, seven and nine.

events.title: Karina Rykman with Roni Kaspi
events.note: A bass player who fronts her own band and plays it like a lead instrument, with Roni Kaspi — one of the most talked-about young drummers anywhere — opening. Doors eight.

events.title: Peach Tree Rascals with Michael Sneed
events.note: San Jose's own, playing the city rather than the suburb they came from. Doors eight.

events.title: Prince vs Michael Jackson DJ Party
events.note: The standing argument, settled by a dance floor, $10. The listing names no room.

events.title: Supertaste with 3kelves
events.note: All ages.

events.title: Sweater Funk Rare Boogie Dance Party
events.note: Fifteen years of boogie 45s nobody else plays, on the Knockout's floor. The best-selected dance night in the city and it has never moved.

events.title: The Infinite Wrench
events.note: Saturday's thirty plays, re-shuffled from Friday's.

events.title: Your Fucked Up Relationship
events.note: The Saturday edition.

events.title: Reggae and Soul Nite
events.note: The late Saturday room at the Kilowatt.

events.title: Armin van Buuren
events.note: Trance in a pier shed at Mission Bay — a warehouse booking at arena scale, listed for completeness.

events.title: Bag Raiders
events.note: Australian nu-disco, one of two Midway rooms tonight.

events.title: Big Star
events.note: Big Star's catalogue performed by a quintet of survivors and admirers — the Memphis band that sold nothing and changed everything. A legacy configuration rather than the band itself, which is why it is not featured, and still one of the best tickets of the week. No time on the mirror.

events.title: DR. GABBA, Narciss and Dazegxd
events.note: Night two of the Bounce festival at Public Works. Times unpublished.

events.title: KAYZO with Domina and hhunter
events.note: Hard dance in the Midway's main room.

events.title: Lucy Bedroque with pinponpanpon
events.note: Second of two Regency nights.

events.title: Madrone x Gamescape Monthly Game Night
events.note: Board games in a bar with a shop supplying them. Free.

events.title: Pinhead Gunpowder with Constant Insult and False Flag
events.note: Billie Joe Armstrong's other band — the one that never stopped sounding like East Bay pop-punk from 1991 — with two local supports.

events.title: Pop Life
events.note: Prince and the adjacent catalogue, free.

events.title: Tamir Hendelman and Tierney Sutton
events.note: A standards duo in the 100-seat Lab, two nights. Found on the Songkick mirror only.

events.title: Daffodil Days Bulb Giveaway
events.note: Up to two hundred free bulbs per household for planting on public land. Applications closed on the 6th; collection is today.

events.title: Paramount Theatre Public Tour
events.note: Two hours inside the greatest art deco interior on the west coast for ten dollars, cash or card, no booking. The Paramount has nothing else on this week, which makes the tour the listing.

events.title: Fig Leaf Gardens Fall Craft Fair
events.note: Handmade goods in an Oakland garden, free, no RSVP.

events.title: Dog Carnival
events.note: Exactly what it says, in Alameda, free.

events.title: Gallery Chat: BeHere / 1942 with Margaret Yee
events.note: An hour in the Great Hall with Margaret Yee on the Japanese American incarceration show — the AR reconstructions of 1942 San Francisco and Oakland work better with someone talking over them. Admission ticket required.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Saturday matinee.

events.title: Kwaidan
events.note: Kobayashi's four ghost stories, the most beautiful horror film ever shot, at half two. Three hours and worth every minute.

events.title: Alameduh Zine Release Party
events.note: A hyperlocal zine launch with DJs and food, free, all ages, on the Alameda waterfront.

events.title: Zero Empty Spaces Berkeley Grand Opening
events.note: Empty downtown retail turned into cheap artist studios, opening to the public for free. The most practical arts project in the East Bay right now.

events.title: HUGEL with Ochok and DERON b2b Darmon
events.note: The closing night of the Greek's 2026 season, which is reason enough. Doors five, show six — early, because the hill after dark in November is not a joke.

events.title: The Sword
events.note: A Japanese swordsmanship film in BAMPFA's autumn run.

events.title: Oakland Comedy Saturday Night
events.note: Two shows, seven and nine, free on limited tickets.

events.title: Dan Ashley
events.note: The local news anchor's rock band, which raises money and does not embarrass itself.

events.title: Free Oakland Symphony Youth String Concert
events.venue: Valley Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: The Oakland Symphony's youth strings, free, on the Holy Names campus. Reserve a ticket.

events.title: Lalo Guerrero Legacy Festival
events.note: Second night of the Guerrero tribute.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Saturday evening.

events.title: Brandi Carlile
events.note: The Burn The Setlist tour — an all-request night, which from a performer this good is a genuinely different show each time. Sold out, doors seven. Take BART; downtown Oakland garages shut their gates and the break-ins are real.

events.title: Super Cassette
events.note: Five dollars, all ages, volunteer-run.

events.title: The Grease Traps and Tori Roze and the Hot Mess
events.note: Deep-funk 45s played by a live band, which is harder than it sounds and they can do it.

events.title: AZ Chike
events.note: Two days after the Brick & Mortar date. Carried by the regional sweep and absent from Cornerstone's own page.

events.title: Alborosie
events.note: The Italian-born, Kingston-based roots reggae producer and singer, in a 150-capacity room. 21+, presented by BMG.

events.title: BeHere / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration
events.note: Dorothea Lange's and Clem Albers's 1942 photographs turned into augmented-reality reconstructions you stand inside. The museum's current special exhibition and the best thing in it. Free this weekend for Bank of America cardholders.

events.title: Covenant
events.note: A preview performance; no curtain time could be confirmed.

events.title: DaBaby and Moneybagg Yo: Bay Area Fest
events.note: A two-day arena rap festival. Listed for completeness.

events.title: The Tannahill Weavers
events.note: Fifty-five years of Scottish traditional music, and the Highland pipes played indoors at close range, which almost nothing else does. They cross the Atlantic rarely and a 300-capacity room is the smallest they play on it. The only outer listing this week that clears the bar for the drive; the Golden Gate toll is southbound only. Doors seven.

events.title: Sunday Assembly Silicon Valley
events.note: A secular congregation that sings pop songs and hears a talk. Free; the listing names no room.

events.title: National STEM Day: Free Admission
events.note: The Tech free all day for National STEM Day. With a four-year-old this is the entire day sorted.

events.title: Autumn in Willow Glen Makers Market
events.note: Free makers market in Willow Glen.

events.title: San Francisco 49ers vs Las Vegas Raiders
events.note: A stadium, deprioritised by the brief, and the reason half the South Bay will be on the 101 all afternoon.

events.title: Sarper Güven
events.note: A two o'clock matinee; waitlist only when this was compiled.

events.title: Tyler Fischer
events.note: The evening headline.

events.title: Helen Hong
events.note: Last of four nights.

events.title: The Smashing Pumpkins
events.note: The Rats In a Cage tour. An arena, listed for completeness.

events.title: Skyline Ridge Trail Hike
events.note: One of the newest trails on the Peninsula, with the bay on one side and the ocean on the other. Free, led.

events.title: Upstairs Downstairs Tour
events.note: The Sunday tour of the house's two halves.

events.title: The Addams Family
events.note: Sunday matinee.

events.title: Orpheus Chamber Orchestra with Isata Kanneh-Mason
events.note: A conductorless orchestra and a pianist who has outgrown the family story, in Home, Suite Home. Half past two in Bing, which is the best-sounding hall on the Peninsula.

events.title: Día de los Muertos at Courthouse Square
events.note: Free altars, music and food on the square, three in the afternoon. Three minutes' walk from Caltrain Redwood City, which genuinely beats driving.

events.title: Fitz and The Tantrums: Picking Up the Pieces in Its Entirety
events.note: The second of two Guild nights, this one the first album start to finish. Doors seven, show eight. Four minutes from Caltrain Menlo Park.

events.title: Leonid & Friends
events.note: The Russian-Ukrainian ensemble who play Chicago's horn charts better than Chicago now can. A tribute act, so never featured, and technically remarkable. Sold through the Fox's own box office; no time published.

events.title: Diwali at the Outer Sunset Farmers Market
events.note: Diwali folded into the Sunday market on 37th Avenue. Free.

events.title: Fort Mason Farmers Market
events.note: Sundays, half nine to half one, on the pier.

events.title: Lower Nob Hill Weekly Cleanup
events.note: Free lunch for volunteers.

events.title: Inner Sunset Flea: Season Finale
events.note: The last Inner Sunset Flea of the year, with Sunset Mercantile. Free, outdoors, on Irving — and the second Sunday slot does not come back until spring.

events.title: Manny's Neighbourhood Trash Cleanup
events.note: A Mission cleanup with $1 beer, free yoga and free fries at the end of it. Sign-up required.

events.title: San Francisco Coffee Festival
events.note: Day two at the Festival Pavilion. From $29.

events.title: Wellness Fest
events.note: Free food tastings and DIY workshops; the listing names no venue. RSVP required.

events.title: Lindy in the Park
events.note: Thirty years of free swing dancing on JFK Drive, every Sunday, with a free lesson at the start. Weather permitting, which in November means check first.

events.title: Blankets and Blockbusters: Toy Story 5
events.note: A free outdoor screening on the plaza, first come first served. Bring the blanket the name promises.

events.title: SF Diwali and Kids Diwali Celebration
events.venue: San Francisco Shri Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir
events.note: A temple-run Diwali with a children's programme, free.

events.title: Studio 8 2026: Babeth Mondini VanLoo
events.note: The Studio 8 Legacy Award programme for the Dutch filmmaker who built a Buddhist broadcaster out of nothing. Half twelve.

events.title: Golden Gate Park Sunday Roller Disco
events.note: Free, outdoors, forty years old, and the sound system is better than most clubs'.

events.title: New People: Being Heumann
events.note: The third open-captioned screening of the Heumann documentary, in Japantown.

events.title: San Francisco Diwali Festival
events.note: The city's largest free Diwali, on the Yerba Buena lawn — dance, music and food, RSVP encouraged but not required. One of four Diwali events this weekend.

events.title: Unwrapped 2026: Queer Tattoo Punk Rock Party and Holiday Mart
events.note: Tattoos, a holiday market and a punk show in El Rio's back garden, which is the most El Rio combination imaginable.

events.title: Los Conductos
events.note: Camilo Restrepo's Colombian feature — a man on the run from a cult, shot on 16mm in almost total darkness. Seventy minutes and unlike anything else.

events.title: Dance Film Fest: Leap
events.note: A free screening with live dance onstage afterwards, suggested donation $10 for children and $15 for adults. The best free family thing in the city today.

events.title: Anime and Manga Club
events.note: Free; the listing names no room.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Sunday matinee.

events.title: SF Symphony: Isabel Leonard Sings Ravel
events.note: The Sunday repeat of the Ravel and Strauss programme, two in the afternoon. Three Davies concerts this week, none of which the Songkick feed this project uses for the hall carries.

events.title: Everything For Sale
events.note: A title opening on Sunday; descriptor withheld rather than guessed.

events.title: How to Clean a House in 10 Easy Steps
events.note: A title in the Sunday run; descriptor withheld rather than guessed.

events.title: Singer Songwriter Sunday
events.note: Five o'clock, in the round, which the Knockout does better than rooms designed for it.

events.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
events.note: The Sunday evening slot.

events.title: Edward Said: Between Worlds
events.note: The Bay Area premiere, in the Arab Film Festival, in the Castro. Doors quarter to five, from $20.

events.title: Diwali on the Square at St. Mark's
events.note: An evening Diwali in a church square, free, RSVP requested, walk-ins welcome.

events.title: Armand Hammer with Sha Ray and DJ Haram
events.note: billy woods and ELUCID, the most demanding rap duo in America, in a 350-cap room that closes at the end of the year. DJ Haram's production underneath. Doors seven, and the second-best ticket in the city tonight.

events.title: Comfort Club, Big Sierra and Danielle Judith
events.note: Three local acts to close the Kilowatt's week.

events.title: Foy Vance with Bonnie Bishop and Ryan McMullan
events.note: Northern Irish soul-folk, big voice, gilded room. Doors six.

events.title: Free Sunday Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP, $20–$25 at the door, two-drink minimum.

events.title: Murray Hill: Showbiz! The Tour
events.note: The self-described hardest-working middle-aged man in showbusiness, seated, in a 1931 nightclub. Doors six, show seven, 21+.

events.title: S.F. Comedy Showcase
events.note: The longest-running weekly showcase in the city, and still where the good sets get tested.

events.title: Reggae Sunday: Champion Reggae Dance Party
events.note: The standing Sunday night.

events.title: Thao & The Get Down Stay Down with Agouti
events.note: A San Francisco band that stopped, and an album-release show for Show Me in the 500-capacity room they grew up in. Sold out, which it was always going to be. Thao Nguyen writes about this city more precisely than anyone currently working in it.

events.title: Triptides with Loco Tranquilo
events.note: Sun-bleached psych pop. All ages.

events.title: North Taurids Meteor Shower Peaks
events.note: The second Taurid peak of the week, and the better one — the North branch throws the fireballs. Look south-east after ten.
Florida rap at double time over beats that sound like a dialling tone. Downstairs, no time published.

events.title: Nia Archives with Bambii
events.note: Jungle, revived by someone young enough to treat it as living music rather than a reference. Bambii supporting makes it a proper night. No time on the mirror.

events.title: Sunday B3 Sessions
events.note: Hammond organ trio, every Sunday, free. The most reliable good hour in the Lower Haight.

events.title: The House That Poems Built
events.note: Poetry in the Madrone, free.

events.title: Contra Costa Vintage Market
events.note: Free vintage market; Lafayette is not a city the brief names, so filed to the East Bay by proximity.

events.title: Free Oakland Up Market
events.note: A free store rather than a market — one free indoor item per person per day.

events.title: Muchos Art and Comic Expo
events.note: Fifty-plus artists, free, at La Peña. The listing's midnight start time is a posting error; treat it as a daytime fair.

events.title: Mapping Utopias
events.note: A programme built around the Some Particular Heaven show.

events.note: The first part of Kobayashi's nine-hour anti-war trilogy. Three hours and twenty minutes, and the best thing BAMPFA will show this year.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Some Particular Heaven
events.note: Ideas of utopia in BAMPFA's own collection, led.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Sunday matinee.

events.title: HellaSecret Speakeasy Comedy
events.note: Free with RSVP in Temescal.

events.note: A big, trained gospel-soul voice in a 400-seat room.
